_comment: Cached Figma variable/node IDs for the wend-ui file, so use_figma pushes and diffs can reference known IDs instead of re-discovering them via a fresh read every time. IDs are stable in Figma once created -- this only goes stale if a variable/node is renamed or deleted outside this workflow. Regenerate with figma-scripts/dump-variable-map.js (paste its contents into a use_figma call) whenever collections change, and spot-check a few IDs with getVariableByIdAsync before trusting a map that's more than a few sessions old.

global._naming_note: As of 2026-09-09 every global variable in this collection is slash-style (color/gray/700, spacing/100, etc.) -- the dash-style gray-700..1000/green/red/yellow entries this note used to describe were renamed to slash-style in a large cleanup pass the same day (see _2026-09-09-rename-pass below). Code's own token names are always dash-style (color-gray-*), so a diff_tokens comparison against this collection's slash-named entries will report those as onlyInProject/onlyInFigma purely from the naming mismatch even when the resolved hex is identical -- normalize slashes to dashes before diffing (see sync-tokens-to-figma skill).
global._yellow_note: Added 2026-09-08, PULLED FROM Figma (variables color/yellow/50 through color/yellow/900, slash-style, VariableID:510:52-61) -- replaces the old amber ramp wholesale, not a rename: Figma authored yellow as an entirely new set of variables with different hex values (e.g. yellow.500 #F5A20B vs amber.500's old #FDA308) and a hue that drifts warmer at higher steps (~48 degrees at 50 down to ~23 degrees at 900) rather than amber/green/red's shared fixed-hue HSL formula. The old amber variables (VariableID:211:18/19, 242:2-9) were NOT deleted -- they were detached from this collection's variableIds (getVariableByIdAsync still resolves several of them directly by ID, e.g. 211:18 still returns name 'color/amber/500'), so they're orphaned clutter in the file rather than a clean removal; a few (211:19, 242:2/3/4/9) return null/undefined even via direct ID lookup, meaning those specific ones actually were deleted. Not cleaned up from the Figma side (the orphaned amber variables still exist, invisible in the normal Variables panel but present in the file) -- code updated every color.amber.N reference to color.yellow.N at the same step number (packages/tokens/tokens/global/color.json, semantic/color.json, semantic/color.dark.json) and adopted Figma's actual yellow hex values rather than keeping the old amber values under a new name. RESOLVED same day: the semantic collection's 3 warning-role variables that still aliased the orphaned amber IDs (color/ui/text/warning VariableID:393:88, color-feedback-warning-background VariableID:49:62, color/ui/border/warning VariableID:393:77 -- 6 mode-bindings total across Light/Dark) were rebound via use_figma's setValueForMode to alias the matching yellow variable at the same step instead (e.g. text/warning Light: amber/800 211:18-family id 242:8 -> yellow/800 510:60). Verified via a fresh read-only scan that no variable in the file aliases any of the 10 old amber IDs anymore.
global._size_note: sizing/0..sizing/3200 (VariableID:357:2 through :357:22, added 2026-08-23 as size/*, renamed in place to sizing/* the same day -- IDs unchanged) is a new code-originated scale, pushed FROM tokens/global/sizing.json TO Figma -- the reverse direction of most entries in this cache. It deliberately duplicates spacing/*'s step names and px values 1:1 (same ALL_SCOPES convention, same slash-style naming) rather than aliasing spacing, per packages/tokens/README.md's Sizing scale section: kept separate so width/height and padding/gap can diverge later even though they're numerically identical today. No Figma component currently binds to sizing/* -- it exists so future width/height properties have a token to reach for.
global._owner_note: sizing/* is the one entry in this collection code created rather than pulled -- everything else here originated in Figma and was pulled into code. Don't assume push-then-verify (steps 2-3 of sync-tokens-to-figma) is unnecessary just because this collection is 'usually' Figma-authoritative. font-size/* below (added 2026-09-09) is a second such entry -- see _fontSizeNote.
global._fontSizeNote: font-size/0 through font-size/3200 (VariableID:545:2 through :545:18, 17 new variables) added 2026-09-09, CODE-FIRST like sizing/* above -- completing tokens/global/typography.json's font.size scale to match spacing/sizing step-for-step (0/25/50/100/125/275/300/400/500/550/600/700/800/1000/1200/1600/3200; 150/175/200/250/350 already existed). Same ALL_SCOPES convention as the pre-existing font-size/* variables. font-size/150 (VariableID:390:25) was already present in Figma from an earlier pull but had never been added to this cache until now -- if a future diff shows it missing, that's why. font-size/175 (14px) is the one step with no spacing/sizing equivalent, predating this alignment effort -- deliberately left as-is, not removed or renamed.

semantic._naming_note: Mixes dash-style (color-text-secondary) and slash-style (color/action/primary-background) by when each variable was added -- same caveat as the global collection's naming note. color/ui/text/disabled and color/ui/text/primary are a separate, divergent pair from code's color-text-disabled/color-text-primary: 'disabled' is a pure rename with an identical value (safe to treat as the same token under a different name), but 'primary' also carries a different color value than what code currently ships (code pulled the value update but deliberately did NOT adopt the 'ui' name -- introducing a new 'ui' taxonomy category isn't registered in validate-color-taxonomy.js; see packages/tokens/README.md's Color scale section and the 2026-08-19 token-pull session notes). color/ui/outline/focus (VariableID:351:81, added 2026-08-23) is a third 'ui'-namespaced variable but WAS pulled into code, as color.border.focus (color-border-focus) under the existing 'border' SELF_EVIDENT_CATEGORY rather than adopting the 'ui' prefix -- same treatment as 'disabled' above, a rename-in-spirit with a code-side name that fits the existing taxonomy. color/ui/foreground and color/ui/border/default (VariableID:360:140, :347:4, both consumed by the new Checkbox component added 2026-08-23) are a fourth and fifth 'ui'-namespaced pair, also pulled into code -- as color.surface.input (color-surface-input) and color.border.input (color-border-input) respectively, again under existing SELF_EVIDENT_CATEGORYs rather than adopting 'ui'. spacing/default, spacing/half, spacing/quarter, spacing/one-plus, spacing/double, spacing/none, and spacing/eighth (this last one added 2026-09-09) exist in Figma with no corresponding token in code at all, by design -- see the 2026-09-09 rename note below for why.
semantic._surfaceCardRemovalNote: 2026-09-09. color-surface-card/color-surface-card-recessed (VariableID:49:55/:49:56) were removed from BOTH sides after being confirmed dead: their values were byte-identical to surface.canvas/surface.canvas-recessed in both light and dark (Figma had authored them as a separate, non-aliased duplicate, not a real distinct color), they had zero variable bindings anywhere in the Figma file (checked every page), and no shipped component referenced them in code -- only the docs site's own chrome did (.wend-nav's background in packages/web-components/src/global/docs.css, and the general-purpose .wend-surface utility class in packages/styles/src/base.css), both now repointed to color-surface-canvas instead. Removed from tokens/semantic/color.json + color.dark.json, removed from Figma via Variable.remove() (safe -- zero bindings confirmed first), removed from this cache. Separately, in the same session, the user renamed the ADJACENT (unrelated) variable color-surface-canvas itself to color/ui/background/canvas in Figma (VariableID:49:53, value unchanged) -- per the established convention already documented in the _naming_note above (don't adopt 'ui'-namespaced Figma names verbatim; map into the existing SELF_EVIDENT_CATEGORY taxonomy instead), code's token keeps its existing name color.surface.canvas (color-surface-canvas) rather than being renamed to match -- flagged to the user rather than silently decided. A future diff_tokens run will show this specific variable's Figma name (color/ui/background/canvas) not matching code's name (color-surface-canvas) even though the value is identical; that's a naming-only mismatch, not a value drift.
semantic._2026-09-09-rename-pass: User did a large batch rename+delete pass across BOTH global and semantic collections the same day as the other 2026-09-09 entries below. Detected by checking all 190 previously-cached VariableIDs directly via getVariableByIdAsync (undefined = deleted; name !== cached name = renamed) rather than trusting name-based diffing alone, since a straight diff_tokens run would have shown ~80 spurious onlyInFigma/onlyInProject pairs from renames alone. RESULTS: 74 pure renames (no value change) -- global gray/green/red/yellow dash-style entries (color-gray-700 etc.) all became slash-style (color/gray/700), and most semantic action/button color variables were restructured from a dash-suffixed style (color/action/primary-background-hover) to a fully-nested slash style with an explicit trailing /default for the base state (color/action/primary/background/hover, color/action/primary/background/default) -- see this collection's updated _naming_note. Per the long-standing convention already documented there and in the sync-tokens-to-figma skill, code's own names stay dash-style-flat (color-action-primary-background, no explicit -default suffix at the semantic tier) rather than mirroring Figma's new nesting -- this is a pure Figma-side reorganization, NOT something to replicate in tokens/**/*.json. This cache's variable-name KEYS were refreshed to the new names (same VariableIDs) so future pushes/lookups use current names; no token JSON changed for the renames themselves. One rename was inconsistent with its siblings and is worth knowing about: color/action/destructive-secondary-background became color/action/destructive/secondary/background (segments split, no /default added) while every sibling (foreground, hover, and the primary/tertiary equivalents) got .../default appended and kept its variant name hyphenated (destructive-secondary/foreground/default) -- looks like a one-off inconsistency in how the rename was applied, not a deliberate distinction; harmless since neither form is adopted in code either way. TWO genuine deletions (not renames -- getVariableByIdAsync returned undefined): (1) VariableID:49:51, was 'color-text-on-primary' -- confirmed zero consumers anywhere in code (no CSS, no other token aliased it), so removed from tokens/semantic/color.json + color.dark.json too (clean two-sided removal, see packages/tokens/README.md's Color scale section). (2) VariableID:350:2, was 'button-icon-only-padding' -- FLAGGED, NOT removed from code: packages/styles/src/components/wend-button.css:85 actively uses `var(--button-icon-only-padding, 10px)` for the icon-only button variant's square padding. Figma deleting this variable might mean the icon-only button variant was intentionally dropped from the Figma component (in which case code should follow and remove the icon-only variant entirely, not just the token), or it might be an unintentional casualty of the batch cleanup -- ask the user which before touching wend-button.css or tokens/component/button.json; the CSS fallback (10px) keeps the current variant working either way in the meantime. ONE genuine value change (not a rename, not a deletion): color/action/destructive-secondary-background's DARK value moved from red.900 (#4F1D17) to red.700 (#93261A) -- background-hover (red.800 dark) was untouched. Pulled into code: tokens/semantic/color.dark.json's action.destructive-secondary.background now aliases {color.red.700}. The button-component tier needed no separate edit since it aliases the semantic leaf directly (tokens/component/button.dark.json's destructive-secondary.background.default -> {color.action.destructive-secondary.background}). Also reconfirmed (unrelated to this pass, already flagged 2026-09-08, still not adopted by design): color-button-primary-foreground-disabled / action.primary.foreground-disabled remains gray.500 both modes in code vs Figma's gray.700 both modes -- this surfaced again as a 'changed' entry in the diff purely because it was never resolved, not because anything new happened to it.
semantic._spacingAliasRenameNote: 2026-09-09, FIGMA-FIRST rename, no value changes: the user renamed Figma's own semantic-spacing aliases in place (same VariableIDs, still aliasing the exact same unchanged global spacing steps) -- spacing/condensed -> spacing/half (still -> spacing/100), spacing/compressed -> spacing/quarter (still -> spacing/50), spacing/expanded -> spacing/one-plus (still -> spacing/300). spacing/default/double/none were not renamed. A brand-new spacing/eighth (VariableID:544:1236, aliasing spacing/25) also appeared, not present in any earlier session's dump. Confirmed via a fresh use_figma read that the GLOBAL spacing/0..spacing/3200 scale itself is completely unchanged (still 21 steps, identical values) -- a formal diff_tokens run against it on 2026-09-09 returned zero `changed` entries. Per the established convention (see packages/tokens/README.md's Spacing scale section and the sync-tokens-to-figma skill), code never tracks this semantic-alias layer as its own token tier -- component tokens reference the global scale directly (e.g. {spacing.100}, not a `spacing.half`/`spacing.condensed` token) -- so this rename requires NO changes to any token JSON or built CSS. The only real work was updating the old alias names to the new ones everywhere they were mentioned by name in this file's own component notes (toggle, help-text, text-area, option/select) and in packages/tokens/README.md's prose.
semantic._state_note: color-action-primary-background-hover was seen at VariableID:49:59 as of this refresh; a much earlier state (pre-2026-08-03) had also recorded it at :49:58, which was actually color/action/primary-background -- if a future diff shows both resolving to the same collection but different keys, trust a fresh dump-variable-map.js run over this cached file.
semantic._borderLightStepNote: 2026-09-08, FIGMA-FIRST: color/ui/border/negative (VariableID:393:75), color/ui/border/positive (:393:76), and color/ui/border/warning (:393:77) each had their Light-mode value moved one ramp step lighter by the user directly in Figma (red.700->red.500, green.800->green.700, yellow.700->yellow.600) -- Dark mode untouched. Pulled into code the same day: tokens/semantic/color.json's color.border.danger/success/warning now alias {color.red.500}/{color.green.700}/{color.yellow.600} instead of the 700/800/700 steps they used before. This also decoupled border.success/warning/danger from text.success/warning/danger, which still sit on their original (unchanged) steps -- the two families no longer share a step number for these three roles, unlike before.
semantic._backgroundWarningNote: 2026-09-08, CODE-FIRST (the reverse of _borderLightStepNote above): color/ui/background/warning (VariableID:390:4) was still a literal RGBA resolving to the OLD amber-500 base (#FDA308) at the alpha values matching light/dark -- it never got updated when the amber ramp was replaced by yellow (see the global collection's _yellow_note). Code's own color-feedback-warning-background-subtle had already been corrected to the new yellow-500 base (#F5A20B) when amber was swapped out; this push brought Figma's literal in line with it via setValueForMode (not an alias -- color/ui/background/positive and color/ui/background/negative, VariableID:384:299 and :390:18, are the same kind of literal-not-alias translucent-pill value and were NOT touched, since only the warning one was reported stale). Verified by reading the value back and reconstituting hex: #f5a20b40 light / #f5a20bb2 dark, byte-exact match to code.
semantic._drift_flag: RESOLVED 2026-09-08. First flagged during the 2026-08-23 Checkbox pull: color/action/primary/background/default and background/hover (and, as a fuller diff_tokens run on 2026-09-08 later confirmed, the same dark-mode divergence across action.secondary/action.tertiary/action.destructive/action.destructive-secondary/action.destructive-tertiary too) resolve to different values per mode in Figma, contradicting the then-documented 'every action.* token is deliberately identical in light and dark mode' design decision. Per explicit user request on 2026-09-08, this was adopted app-wide -- tokens/semantic/color.dark.json now has a full action.* block (primary/secondary/tertiary/destructive/destructive-secondary/destructive-tertiary background+foreground overrides) matching Figma's dark values, and packages/tokens/README.md's Color scale section was rewritten to describe the new flip-by-mode behavior instead of the old fixed-appearance one. NOT adopted at the time: action.primary.foreground/-foreground-disabled and action.destructive.foreground stayed fixed both modes (gray.50/gray.500) -- Figma's dark values for those three (gray.975/gray.700/gray.975) pair with a DIFFERENT light value too (gray.25 vs code's gray.50, gray.700 vs code's gray.500), so adopting just the dark side would've been a guess at how to reconcile the light-mode gap as well; left flagged rather than silently resolved. The checkbox's own checked-state tokens still alias action.primary directly, so they now inherit the dark-mode divergence for free -- no checkbox-specific change was needed. FOLLOW-UP same day: a user caught this in practice -- the primary button's dark-mode text rendered as near-white (gray.50, #FAF9F9) instead of Figma's near-black (gray.975, #1A1A1A). Reported directly with the expected hex, so action.primary.foreground (and action.destructive.foreground, which aliases it) was fixed to match Figma fully: gray.25 light / gray.975 dark, both modes now, not just dark. action.primary.foreground-disabled is unchanged (gray.500 both modes) -- not reported, still flagged; note Figma's own foreground-disabled value (gray.700) is fixed both modes too (not a mode-dependent gap like foreground was), just a different single value than code's.

nodes._comment: Canvas nodes bound to semantic/component variables or component properties -- useful when a collection rebuild requires rebinding fills/strokes/fontFamily/etc, or when re-touching the button's icon slots.
nodes._pages_note: As of 2026-08-25 the file has multiple pages (Button, Checkbox, Toggle, Radio, Help Text, Text Input, Text Area, plus Cover/Typography/Color/Icons/reference pages not tracked here) -- the single 'page': "Button" field below predates that and is stale/button-specific; don't assume it names the only page. Page IDs: Button=10:2, Checkbox=347:2, Toggle=367:164, Radio=374:187 (also hosts the separate 'Radio Group' component, node 374:231, alongside the Radio COMPONENT_SET), Help Text=384:292, Text Input=382:232, Text Area=404:105. Get a fresh list with `figma.root.children.map(p => ({id: p.id, name: p.name}))`.
nodes._rename_flag: As of the 2026-08-24 Help Text / Text Input pull, the variable this cache recorded as 'color/ui/text/primary' (VariableID:337:1707) now reads 'color/ui/text/primary-default' in Figma -- same ID, so every alias pointing at it (color.text.primary in code) still resolves correctly; this looks like an in-place Figma rename (adding the '-default' suffix once positive/warning/negative siblings were added, presumably for symmetry) rather than a new variable. Not renamed in code -- 'color.text.primary' has no state axis of its own in the codebase taxonomy, and 'default' would be a stray no-op suffix on a SELF_EVIDENT_CATEGORY leaf, which the taxonomy validator explicitly rejects at the semantic tier. Flagged for awareness only; the naming map above still keys this variable as 'color/ui/text/primary' since a future dump-variable-map.js refresh needs to catch the rename, not this note.

radioGroup._note: Added 2026-08-23. A single (non-variant) COMPONENT, not a COMPONENT_SET -- lives on the same page as the base Radio component but is a separate top-level node (374:231), not a child of the Radio COMPONENT_SET (374:188). Structure: an optional 'Label' text node (font-size.175, color.text.primary -- same style as the group's own label prop in code) + 5 instances of the base Radio component (all placeholder 'Selected=False, State=Default', i.e. no example of a selected state), in a VERTICAL auto-layout frame with itemSpacing=16 (spacing/default=16=spacing.200) applied uniformly to every gap including label-to-first-radio. Each Radio instance exposes 'Show Label#360:32' (BOOLEAN, default true) as a component property on the base Radio component itself -- missed when wend-radio was first built, but not actually a functional gap: wend-radio already hides its label whenever the `label` prop is an empty string, which is equivalent in effect. wend-radio-group is NOT a literal transcription of this Figma node (which just shows 5 static radio instances) -- it's a data-driven wrapper: consumers slot in their own <wend-radio> children (native `shadow:false` Stencil components support <slot> content relocation despite not using a real shadow root), and the group propagates `name`/`disabled` and computes each child's `selected` by comparing its `value` to the group's own `value` prop, re-emitting a consolidated wendChange with the newly selected value whenever a child reports selection. Uses a native <fieldset disabled={disabled}> wrapper so the browser's own form-disabling cascades to the slotted <input>s as a functional safety net, in addition to code explicitly propagating `.disabled` to each wend-radio child for the correct visual (dimmed) treatment (native fieldset-disabling alone doesn't trigger wend-radio's own CSS dimming, which keys off its own `disabled` prop/class, not the native :disabled pseudo-class).

radio._note: Added 2026-08-23. 4 variants (Selected=False/True x State=Default/Hover), no Disabled -- same shape as checkbox (code added a disabled prop anyway, dimmed via CSS opacity, for family consistency; not Figma-verified). Same width/height (58x20 including label) and Label-node structure as checkbox, and reuses the same outer-ring tokens (color.surface.input / color.border.input, VariableID:360:140 / :347:4) -- but unlike checkbox, the outer ring is IDENTICAL across all 4 variants (verified: unselected-hover's ring has the exact same fill/stroke boundVariables as unselected-default), so color.radio.control has only ever needed a 'default' state, no 'hover' variant at all. The inner dot (12x12, bound to sizing/150 -- a real binding, unlike checkbox/radio's own 20px size which is NOT bound) only exists as a child node when Selected=True; code always renders it and toggles visibility via CSS `input:checked ~ .control .dot { visibility: visible }` rather than conditionally in JSX -- native radio-group deselection (browser unchecking a sibling <input> when another radio in the same `name` group is picked) does NOT fire a change event on the deselected sibling, so a JSX-conditional dot (the pattern used for checkbox's checkmark) would have gone stale showing a dot on a radio the browser already deselected. Label text color introduces a new semantic leaf, text.hover (VariableID:374:207, 'color/ui/text/hover' in Figma, light gray.950 dark gray.100) -- used for both the dot's hover fill AND the unselected-label's hover fill, but NOT for the selected-label's hover fill, which oddly reuses color.border.input (VariableID:347:4) instead -- replicated exactly as authored despite reading like a possible Figma authoring slip (a border-role variable used for text), not silently 'corrected' to text.hover for consistency.

toggle._note: Added 2026-08-23. 6 variants (State=Default/Hover/Disabled x On=False/True), no Disabled+Hover combo -- same coverage gap as checkbox/button. No label/text node in any variant (unlike checkbox, which has one) -- code's wend-toggle is a bare switch, no label prop; if a labeled variant is wanted later, check whether Figma has been updated with one before inventing typography tokens for it. Track width(40)/height(24) and the checked-thumb size(18) are NOT variable-bound in Figma (verified via boundVariables) -- code stores them as literal px values in component/toggle.json rather than force-fitting them onto sizing-scale steps that happen to match numerically (unlike the unchecked-thumb size, 16px, which IS bound to sizing/200 and does alias it). The checked track's background/hover/disabled colors reuse the EXISTING color.action.primary.background/-hover/-disabled tokens (same ones button/checkbox already use) -- same known drift applies here as the checkbox _drift_flag below (Figma's action.primary tokens now resolve differently per dark mode than what's shipped in code; not adopted). The unchecked track's default/hover colors are new toggle-specific semantic leaves (action.toggle-unchecked.background/-hover, VariableID:369:167/:369:172) since there was no existing token to reuse for that role. Track border reuses color.border.input (same as checkbox); disabled border/thumb color reuses color.text.disabled (VariableID:231:11, the same variable already cached above as color/ui/text/disabled) rather than introducing a new token. The thumb's soft drop-shadow (color/gray/600, radius 4, offset 0/0) is present on every variant except Default-Off and Disabled-Off in Figma -- reproduced in CSS as a box-shadow shown on :hover (unchecked) and always when checked, which covers exactly those states without a new state axis in the token set.

checkbox._note: Added 2026-08-23. Only 4 variants exist (Checked=False/True x State=Default/Hover) -- no Disabled or Active/Focus variants in Figma. Code added a disabled prop (dimmed via CSS opacity, mirroring the button's pattern) and a :focus-visible ring (reusing color.border.focus) beyond what's in Figma, for accessibility parity with wend-button -- neither is Figma-verified, flag if Figma later adds explicit Disabled/Focus variants so code can be reconciled against real values instead of an inference. The unchecked box's fill/stroke bindings are IDENTICAL between Default and Hover states (both resolve to color/ui/foreground and color/ui/border/default) -- Figma has not yet differentiated an unchecked-hover appearance, so CSS has no unchecked:hover rule either; only checked:hover (background-hover) is styled, matching what's actually authored.

helpText._note: Added 2026-08-24. 4 variants, one axis ('Type': Default/Success/Warning/Error), no boolean properties. Default has no background, just color/ui/text/primary-default text; Success/Warning/Error each get a translucent tinted pill background (color/ui/background/positive|warning|negative, all resolved as an 8-digit hex with alpha -- e.g. positive is #27B07040 light / #27B07080 dark, same green.600 base both modes just at 25%/50% alpha) plus a solid, non-translucent text color (color/ui/text/positive|warning|negative). Pulled into code as color.text.success/warning/danger + color.feedback.success/warning/danger.background-subtle (see packages/tokens/README.md's Color token naming section) -- renamed from Figma's 'positive'/'negative' to the codebase's existing 'success'/'danger' vocabulary, but the component's own `type` prop/variant keeps Figma's exact naming (`error`, not `danger`) since that's what the Figma component itself calls it. wend-help-text is used both standalone and as a child instance inside wend-text-input (see textInput below) -- same cross-component-embedding pattern as wend-button embedding wend-icon.

requiredMarker._note: Added 2026-08-24, CODE-FIRST -- the reverse direction of everything else in this file (which was pulled FROM Figma INTO code). wend-text-input's `required` prop was added in code first with no Figma precedent, then pushed into Figma via use_figma to keep the two in sync, per the user's explicit request. Structure per variant: the existing 'Label' text node was moved out of the COMPONENT's direct children into a new 'Label Row' horizontal auto-layout frame (itemSpacing=2, matching text-input-required-marker-gap/{spacing.25}) inserted at the same index (0) the Label used to occupy; a new '*' text node (Funnel Sans Regular 14px, same font as Label, fill bound to color/ui/text/negative == VariableID:393:86, the SAME variable already used for the Error state's border/help-text -- code's color.text.danger) was appended as the row's second child. The 'Show Label#393:0' visibility binding was MOVED from the Label text node onto the new Label Row frame (so hiding the label hides the marker with it, not leaving a lone asterisk) -- the Label text node itself now has no visibility binding of its own (always visible when its row is). The asterisk's own visibility is bound to the new 'Required#402:0' property independently, default false, matching code's `required` default. Label's layoutSizingHorizontal changed from FILL to HUG (it now hugs within the row instead of filling the old direct parent) and the new Label Row got layoutSizingHorizontal=FILL in its place, so the field/help-text below remain unaffected and the frame's overall width/height (538x605 for the component set) did not change. Applied identically across all 5 variants: Default (row=402:7, asterisk=402:8), Focus (row=402:9, asterisk=402:10), Success (row=402:11, asterisk=402:12), Warning (row=402:13, asterisk=402:14), Error (row=402:15, asterisk=402:16) -- Label node IDs unchanged (383:235, 393:29, 393:70, 393:80, 393:99), just reparented.

textInput._note: Added 2026-08-24. 5 variants on one axis ('State': Default/Focus/Success/Warning/Error) plus three boolean component properties (Show Label, Show Help Text, Required -- all default false except Show Label/Show Help Text which default true) -- unlike radio's redundant 'Show Label' (see radio._note above), Show Label/Show Help Text ARE the only way to hide the label/help-text in this component (wend-text-input has no other signal to derive visibility from, since `label`/`help-text` being an empty string already independently hides each), so both were pulled into code as real props (`showLabel`/`showHelpText`) rather than treated as redundant; `required` is the one exception in this file that went code -> Figma instead (see requiredMarker above). Each State instance contains: a 'Label Row' frame (added 2026-08-24, see requiredMarker) wrapping the 'Label' text node (font-size.175, color/ui/text/primary-default -- reused, not a new variable) plus the required-marker asterisk, an 'Input Field' frame (40px tall, color/ui/foreground background == color.surface.input, 1px color/ui/border/default border == color.border.input, containing a 'Value' text node in the same color/ui/text/primary-default), and a 'Help Text' instance child (390:23 in the Default variant) below it. Figma's Focus differs from Default only by a 2px border (still color.border.input, not a new color) -- not variable-bound in Figma (a raw Tailwind `border-2` in the reference code) -- so it was NOT pulled in as a 5th `state` enum value, AND its border-thickening mechanic was deliberately not reproduced even for the CSS `:focus-within` case: changing `border-width` still shifts the field's inner content by a pixel (the classic 'wiggle') even under `box-sizing: border-box`. Code instead adds an `outline` (`text-input-focus-outline-color/-width/-offset`, aliasing the shared `color.border.focus` token, same convention as button/checkbox/toggle/radio's own focus rings) on `:focus-within`, which sits outside the box and never affects layout -- see packages/tokens/README.md's Color token naming section. A focused input keeps showing whichever validation-state border color (`state` prop) is already active plus the outline ring on top, a Default+Focus / Success+Focus / etc. combination Figma's own variant axis doesn't enumerate. Success/Warning/Error change ONLY the field's border color (color.border.success/warning/danger) plus swap in a tinted Help Text instance (type=success/warning/error) below -- the field's background and the typed value's text color stay constant across every state. `color/ui/border/default` here is the SAME Figma variable already cached above as checkbox/radio/toggle's shared form-control border (VariableID:347:4) -- despite its Figma name literally saying 'default', it is NOT code's `color.border.default` (gray.700); it's `color.border.input` (gray.800), per the established precedent for this specific variable.
textInput._disabledFlag: Added 2026-08-25, CODE-FIRST like requiredMarker above -- code already had a fully-implemented `disabled` prop (dimmed via CSS `opacity: 0.5` on the outer <label>, matching the button/checkbox/radio precedent) with no Figma equivalent; this pushed a matching 'State=Disabled' variant into Figma to keep the two in sync, per explicit user request. Implementation: cloned the 'State=Default' component (393:26), renamed to 'State=Disabled', set `opacity = 0.5` on the cloned top-level COMPONENT node (mirrors code's single opacity rule on the whole subtree -- no per-child color changes, unlike button/toggle's dedicated *-background-disabled/*-foreground-disabled tokens), positioned at (20, 605) as a 6th row, and grew the component set frame from 538x605 to 538x722. GOTCHA hit during this push: `ComponentNode.clone()` on a node whose parent is a COMPONENT_SET does NOT insert the clone back into that set -- Figma silently reparents the clone onto the PAGE instead (presumably because the clone starts out with a duplicate 'State=Default' name, which would be an invalid duplicate variant within the set). The clone has to be explicitly moved back in via `componentSet.appendChild(clone)` AFTER renaming it to a unique variant name -- verified by re-reading `cs.componentPropertyDefinitions().State.variantOptions` before and after the appendChild call; only after the appendChild did 'Disabled' actually appear in that list. New node id: 409:12. The new Disabled variant keeps Default's Help Text sub-instance (neutral/untinted) and its existing Show Label/Show Help Text/Required bindings unchanged -- Figma's variant axis can't represent every state x disabled combination (same limitation already documented for Focus above), so this single Disabled row is a Default+disabled baseline only, not a disabled variant of Success/Warning/Error too.

textArea._note: Added 2026-08-25. Figma-authored as a duplicate of the Text Input component set AFTER the 2026-08-24 code-first `required` push -- its 'Label Row'/'*' marker structure and the 'Show Label#393:0'/'Show Help Text#393:3'/'Required#402:0' component-property IDs are identical to Text Input's for exactly that reason (same lineage, not a coincidence or a real cross-component dependency). Pulled 100% FROM Figma INTO code this time (the normal direction, unlike Text Input's required-marker) -- no new semantic or component color tokens were needed anywhere; every color.text-area.* token aliases the exact same leaves color.text-input.* does. Two real differences from Text Input, both intentional per Figma's own authoring: (1) the field is 88px tall (sizing.1000, fixed, not the 40px sizing.500 single-line height) and (2) its horizontal padding is spacing.100/8px (Figma's 'spacing/half', renamed 2026-09-09 from 'spacing/condensed' -- same VariableID, same value) rather than Text Input's spacing.200/16px ('spacing/default') -- vertical padding (spacing.50/4px) matches. Each Input Field also contains a 'Resize Handle' frame (404:106 in Default, a small absolutely-positioned image referencing a diagonal-lines resize-grip asset) in the bottom-right corner -- NOT reproduced in code as an image: a native <textarea> with CSS `resize: vertical` already renders the browser's own resize gripper in that exact corner, which is functionally correct (actually resizable) where a static image wouldn't be, so no asset was downloaded/imported for this. Figma's Focus variant is the same 2px-same-color-border pattern as Text Input's (not variable-bound, a raw `border-2`) and was handled identically: not pulled in as a 5th `state` value, reproduced instead via the same `text-area-focus-outline-*` outline-on-:focus-within convention (not border-thickening, to avoid the 'wiggle' -- see Text Input's own note above and packages/tokens/README.md). Each variant's Label Row already carries both the 'Show Label#393:0' visibility binding (on the row) and its child '*' marker's own 'Required#402:0' visibility binding, exactly matching the structure Text Input was left in after its required-marker push -- code's wend-text-area component mirrors wend-text-input's render() 1:1 for this part (label span + conditional required-marker span), just swapping the single-line <input> for a <textarea>.
textArea._disabledFlag: Added 2026-08-25, CODE-FIRST -- same push as Text Input's disabled variant (see textInput._disabledFlag above), applied identically: cloned 'State=Default' (404:112), renamed 'State=Disabled', `opacity = 0.5` on the clone, positioned at (20, 990) as a 6th row, component set frame grown from 538x1003 to 538x1185 (990 + 145 height + 50 bottom margin, matching this file's existing -- larger than Text Input's -- bottom padding). Hit the exact same `clone()`-reparents-to-page gotcha documented in Text Input's note; fixed the same way (`componentSet.appendChild(clone)` after renaming). New node id: 409:422. Same 'Default+disabled baseline only' caveat applies -- no disabled variant of Success/Warning/Error was created.

option._note: Added 2026-09-08. 3 variants on one axis ('State': Default/Hover/Selected), plus boolean props Icon Left/Icon Right/Slot Left/Slot Right and two SLOTs ('Slot' for a checkbox/toggle, 'Slot 2' on the right) -- all for a possible future multi-select variant, none used by the current single-select pull (deliberately out of scope, see packages/tokens/README.md). Padding aliases spacing/half+spacing/quarter (renamed 2026-09-09 from spacing/condensed+spacing/compressed, same VariableID:320:1334/:320:1335, code: spacing.100/spacing.50 -- NOT the parallel semantic-spacing names, see the established 'reference the global scale directly' convention already documented for toggle's calc() tokens); corner radius aliases a NEW variable 'radius/selection' (VariableID:497:310) which itself aliases global radius/regular (VariableID:49:28, code: radius.regular) -- 'selection' here is just Figma's own alias-of-an-alias, not a second radius value, so code aliases radius.regular directly rather than inventing a redundant intermediate name. Hover fill aliases a NEW variable 'color/selection/background/hover' (VariableID:418:281 -> global gray.100, VariableID:211:4); Selected fill aliases a NEW variable 'color/selection/background/selected' (VariableID:418:283 -> global gray.200, VariableID:211:5) -- both pulled into code as color.selection.option.background-hover/-selected (see README's new 'selection' role-based category). Value text color aliases color/ui/text/primary-default (VariableID:337:1707, same as every other component's plain label -- code: color.text.primary). The left 'Slot' (VariableID:497:289, unused) pads to 'spacing/none' (VariableID:136:2, i.e. 0) -- confirms it's a reserved-but-empty slot for the multi-select checkbox, not currently contributing any spacing.

selectionPanel._note: Added 2026-09-08. A single COMPONENT (not a COMPONENT_SET -- no variants), unlike every other top-level component in this file. Fill aliases color/ui/foreground (VariableID:360:140, the SAME variable already cached above as checkbox/toggle/radio/text-input's shared form-control surface -- code: color.surface.input); corner radius aliases radius/medium (VariableID:49:29, code: radius.medium); padding on all sides aliases spacing/50 (VariableID:49:32, code: spacing.50). Has a DROP_SHADOW effect (rgba(51,51,51,0.2), blur 2, y-offset 1, NOT variable-bound -- a genuinely new visual treatment, no prior component in this file has a shadow effect besides toggle's thumb, which uses a bound color variable rather than a raw effect) -- pulled into code as the literal select.panel.shadow token (see README), following the same 'unbound literal, not force-aliased' precedent as text-input-border-width. The base component's own itemSpacing=10 auto-layout property does NOT match the actual rendered example inside Select's Focus state (see select.structure.focus below) -- the embedded instance packs its 5 Option children with zero visible gap (5 x 26px = 130px = the panel's own slot height, an exact arithmetic match), so itemSpacing=10 was treated as vestigial and NOT reproduced in code; option has no gap token.

select._note: Added 2026-09-08. Same lineage as Text Area's own 'duplicated from Text Input' origin -- identical Show Label/Show Help Text/Required property IDs, same 6-state axis (Default/Focus/Success/Warning/Error/Disabled), same border-color variable bindings (color/ui/border/default|positive|warning|negative|disabled -- see textInput's own note above for these variables' cached IDs; disabled is a NEW binding not used by Text Input's own Disabled variant, which relies on plain opacity in code -- Select follows the SAME opacity convention per explicit user decision, does NOT adopt this bound disabled-border color). Two real differences from Text Input: (1) the field shows a chevron icon (wend-icon-chevron-down default, wend-icon-chevron-up when State=Focus) instead of a typed value -- the icon instance has no bound fill, inherits color like every other wend-icon usage; (2) State=Focus (node 418:237) embeds a 'Selection Panel' instance directly below the field (see select.structure.focus), which is what makes this a listbox-style single-select rather than a native <select> or a searchable/typeahead combobox -- no search input exists anywhere in the design. Figma's Focus variant is also a thicker (2px vs 1px) same-color border, same 'not reproduced, use an outline instead' treatment as every other *-focus-outline-* token in this file.

focus._note: Selection Panel instance (node 519:129) sits at (0, 70) inside State=Focus, 4px below the Input Field's bottom edge (field: y=26 h=40 -> bottom=66; panel: y=70 -> gap=4px = spacing.50, pulled into code as select.panel.offset). Contains 5 Option instances (I519:129;518:67;520:172 through ;520:176) stacked with zero gap -- the first one is Figma's 'Selected' example (right-side wend-icon-check-solid visible), the rest are plain 'Default' rows (left/right icons hidden) -- confirms single-select semantics: exactly one option shown as selected via checkmark, not multi-select checkboxes. This 5-option example is view-only reference content, not itself pulled into any token or component structure -- the actual wend-select renders whatever wend-option children the consumer slots in.

chip._note: Added 2026-09-09 (user's own code scaffold existed first -- src/components/wend-chip/wend-chip.tsx and an empty wend-chip.css -- but the .tsx never returned its render() JSX and the CSS had no content; both fixed as part of this pull, not carried over). 3-variant State axis (Default/Hover/Disabled) plus two independent booleans: Focus (toggles the 'focus ring' frame's visibility, 74x28 vs the pill's own 70x24 -- a 2px offset on every side, matching the button/checkbox/toggle/radio 1px-width/2px-offset focus-outline convention, NOT text-input/select's flush 0-offset style) and 'Close action' (toggles the wend-icon-close-solid instance's visibility -- pulled into code as the `closable` prop, default true matching Figma). Root fill: Default and Disabled BOTH alias VariableID:49:53 (color/ui/background/canvas, code: color.surface.canvas) -- identical value, no separate disabled-background token; Hover aliases VariableID:418:281 (color/selection/background/hover), the exact same variable option.row.background.hover already uses -- code reuses {color.selection.option.background-hover} directly rather than adding a new leaf, since Figma itself treats this as one shared variable, not two coincidentally-equal ones. Label + close-icon color: VariableID:337:1707 (color/ui/text/primary/default, code: color.text.primary) for Default/Hover, VariableID:231:11 (code: color.text.disabled) for Disabled -- a real color change, not opacity-dimming, so code pulls color.text.disabled directly. Close icon is an INSTANCE of wend-icon-close-solid (16x16, code: chip.icon-size = sizing.200) -- already fixed to a filled path earlier this same session (see the icons._note above), so its fill-based coloring here needed no special handling. IMPORTANT CAVEAT surfaced to the user, not silently changed: chip.background.default aliases the SAME token (surface.canvas) this docs site itself uses as its own page background, so a resting/disabled chip renders with no visible fill on packages/web-components/src/docs/**/*.html specifically (canvas-on-canvas) -- correct per Figma's actual bound variable (confirmed via a direct get_screenshot of node 565:2457, which DOES show a visible pill against Figma's own white canvas), just a cross-context contrast gap between Figma's preview background and this site's page background. No component-tier border/stroke on the pill itself -- only the focus-ring frame has a stroke.

comboBox._note: Added 2026-09-11. Same lineage as Text Input/Select's own 'duplicated from Text Input' origin -- identical Show Label/Show Help Text/Required property IDs, same 6-state axis. Input Field (544:901, 498x40 in the example, fill=VariableID:360:140=color/ui/foreground=code.surface.input, border=VariableID:347:4=code.border.input, radius 8=radius.medium) contains a real Figma SLOT (565:2406, the 'Slot#565:8' property) holding selected options as `chip` INSTANCES (State=Default, the exact same wend-chip component pulled 2026-09-09) -- confirms the 'selected option renders as a chip inside the input' spec directly from the file rather than the verbal description alone. Also contains a small icon row: wend-icon-remove-circle (clear-all, VariableID:337:1707=code.text.primary, same as chevron) + wend-icon-chevron-down/up. Border colors match text-input/select exactly: success=393:76(border.success), warning=393:77(border.warning), error=393:75(border.danger); Disabled binds a DISTINCT color/ui/border/disabled (VariableID:406:217, resolves to VariableID:211:12=gray/700 both modes) -- same variable already flagged and NOT adopted for Select's own Disabled variant; combo-box follows the same opacity-dimming-only precedent, no new border-disabled token. Dropdown rows: the embedded Selection Panel instance's Option children each have a 'Slot Left' (Slot#497:12, visibility Slot Left#497:16) populated with a Checkbox INSTANCE (Checked=False/True, State=Default -- the exact same wend-checkbox component/variables) -- this is the Slot Left prop Option's own build (2026-09-08) explicitly left unimplemented ('no checkbox/toggle slot support in v1 ... skip until asked'); pulled into code as wend-option's new `multi` boolean prop, reusing the existing checkbox.*/color.checkbox.* tokens directly rather than adding new option-scoped leaves, since Figma's embedded Checkbox instances are bound to the same variables wend-checkbox already aliases. Row background hover/selected still the same color/selection/background/hover|selected (418:281/418:283) wend-option already used for single-select. THREE deliberate deviations from Figma's static single-frame example, all flagged rather than silently decided (see packages/tokens/README.md's combo-box paragraph for the full reasoning): chip row wraps (Figma authors layoutWrap=NO_WRAP on both the Input Field and its chip Slot, itemSpacing 10/8 respectively -- only reads correctly because the example never has more than 2 chips); clear-all only renders when values.length > 0 (Figma's static frames show wend-icon-remove-circle visible even in the empty Disabled example, which has 0 chips and nothing to clear); chevron direction tracks the live isOpen runtime state rather than the state-variant name (cross-variant chevron sample: Default/Disabled show chevron-down, Focus/Success/Warning/Error all show chevron-up -- an artifact of which state each static frame happened to be left in, not a real rule -- confirmed by comparing all 6 variants' chevron + Selection Panel visibility directly rather than assuming from names).

icons._comment: Icon components live on the 'Icons' page, nested inside per-category FRAMEs (arrows/user interface/layout & format/etc), not as flat top-level COMPONENT nodes. figma-scripts/fetch-icon-inventory.js's old flat page.children.filter(...) scan returned [] against the real file for this reason -- fixed 2026-09-09 to use page.query('COMPONENT, COMPONENT_SET') (recursive) instead, which covers both the flat and categorized layouts.

wend-icon-close-solid._note: 2026-09-09: the user redesigned this icon directly in Figma from a bold filled X to a thin 2px stroke X (path 'M18 6L6 18M6 6L18 18', stroke='#1A1A1A', stroke-width 2, round caps/joins). A stroke would have made this the ONLY icon in the set not using a filled fill="" path, breaking the color/currentColor override every consumer relies on (get-icon-svg.mjs only string-replaces fill="currentColor"; a hardcoded stroke color ignores the `color` prop). First reconciled code-side only, via a throwaway clone + VectorNode.outlineStroke() (converts the stroke to a pixel-identical filled outline) without touching the real Figma component. The user then did the equivalent themselves directly on the real component -- its child vector (still named 'Vector (Stroke)', a leftover from Figma's own outline-stroke operation) is now fill: SOLID #1A1A1A with no stroke, geometry matching the code-side reconciliation almost exactly (sub-0.0001 floating-point differences in the exported path, e.g. 5.29295 vs the earlier hand-derived 5.29297). packages/icons/src/svg/wend-icon-close-solid.svg was updated to Figma's exact re-exported path (fill="") and rebuilt into dist/ -- both sides are fill-based now, so (unlike the note this replaces) there is no longer an expected permanent diff_icons mismatch here; a future diff_tokens-style check should show this icon clean.
